title: Duke's call about My People and conducting in Chicago
summary: Duke phoned from Canada to send Jones to conduct the second Ellington band and choir at McCormick Place in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He was working on what, "Timon of Athens", then, in Canada?
Yeah, that's right, that's the name of it.
Uh-huh.
And I was at home and you know how he can speak in an oblique way.
Oh, yes.

It's never quite direct, you know. So he says, "Hey, James, this is Eddie Ellington." I said, "Hi, Edward, how do you feel?" So he says, "I have some singers I want you to take a look at," and it was Lil Greenwood, Jimmy Grissom, Joya Sherrill (PHONETIC). When I wound up I was out of town. I was back on the road, in Chicago. I left
New York, you know? So he says -- then there was a choir there that I had to work with, you know, and the next thing I knew I was in McCormack -- it was McCormack Place in Chicago.
Uh-huh.
And I was conducting -- it was a great show, though. It was one of the high points of my career, I think, you know.
And did you put together that band or did Duke put it together?
No, Duke --
It was like the second string Ellington Band or the other Ellington Band, right?
Yeah, it was band number two.
And it had almost everybody in it -- or was everybody in it an alumnus?

Yeah. And Duke and I -- see, what he would do, when he came back to New York, he was working at Basin Street East on weekends, but during the week he would fly out to Chicago, and then he would take Strayhorn one time and he would take me the other time.
Uh-huh.
You know, so we could all get our wits together on what we were going to do.
In Chicago you were conducting and Strayhorn was playing the piano, is that right?
No, I was playing piano too.
Oh. Well, Strayhorn was involved in it, wasn't he?

He did some writing, you know. Some of the writing -- we used some things out of, "Paris Blues," and "Black, Brown and Beige." He just went in the book -- and then Duke -- the old man wrote some more things.
But he was good at borrowing from himself.
Yeah. Oh, he did. He did, beautifully. So that's the only time I didn't have time to take a drink, because that was an athletic event, as a conductor.
